why: A weight the User stated is used as it stands, and nothing is assumed.
A food the Coach cannot match is kept anyway and named as uncounted. It never sends the Turn to clarify: clarify is the graph's one interrupt, and meal logging is not it.
message: I ate a bowl of zzzfoodzzz

why: Dinuguan is in no external food catalogue this system reaches. The local Filipino dish table is the only thing that can count it, and it is consulted before any external call.
A proxy row is a canned product standing in for a home-cooked dish. That is a marking the User depends on, so it may not be lost to a Coach being brief.
The correction the previous answer invited. The Item is corrected in place, so the day it counts against does not move.
given: I ate a bowl of zzzfoodzzz
message: sorry, that zzzfoodzzz was actually pinakbet

why: A day with nothing counted says so rather than reporting zeros.
The review is summed out of PostgreSQL, not out of the checkpoint.
The Thread never restarts and it is not where a Meal lives, so an earlier day is answered from the same place as today.
The gap is computed in SQL, the filters run in SQL, and only then does a model rank what survived. The Recommendation is written down so it can be accepted later.
A disliked food is struck out in SQL before a model sees a candidate, so it cannot be ranked back in.
message: what should I eat next to hit my goal?

why: The User changes a stable fact by saying it, and the write goes to PostgreSQL and nowhere else.
The Goal is a body-weight target, and this is the number it is measured against.
An allergy statement adds to the list rather than replacing it, and the next Turn reads the changed Profile.
A diet pattern is what the candidate filter reads to strike conflicting foods out.
The mixed-intent path. The Meal is written first and the question is answered from a day total that already holds it — which is the whole reason the order matters.
message: I had tinola for dinner, is that enough protein for one meal?

why: The second Intent reads what the first produced: the Profile the recommender filters on is the one this Turn just changed, not the one it was a moment ago. No allergen-absence assertion belongs here — the update_profile confirmation names the allergen on purpose, which is why that Intent is not allergy-checked at all. The absence claim is the draft Recommendation case in the safety group.
message: add shrimp to my allergies, and then tell me what to eat tonight

why: The clarify path, reached the way it usually is: the router is not confident enough to classify the message at all, so the Coach asks rather than guessing.
A Profile statement the extractor cannot pin to one field is a question to the User, not a guessed field.
message: I think I am a bit heavier than I was
